A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Advancing Expert Specialization for Better MoE. All 36 pages, including Appendices A-K, support comparison. Scientific text and rendered content match; differences are confined to version identifiers and author metadata.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark experiments in Table 1, loss ablations and routing analyses in Figures 2-4, and additional experiments and timing measurements in Appendices H-J.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, supplementary evaluations, and training-time measurements reported in v4.

M1.justification: The orthogonality and variance losses, their combination with auxiliary load balancing, and the optimization procedure are identical in Section 3 and Appendices C and H.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 11 mathematical, multidomain, and coding benchmarks, training sources, and evaluation scenarios. The mixed Numina/GPQA/HumanEval training experiment in Appendix H.3 is already present in v4.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains With Aux Loss, Loss-Free Balancing, GShard, and ST-MoE. Table 7 retains ERNIE 4.5 LBL and SIMBAL, and the base-model and auxiliary-loss comparisons in the other appendix tables also match.

E3.justification: Sample counts, three-epoch training budgets, model and LoRA configurations, metrics, zero-shot evaluation, and generation-length settings are unchanged. The mixed-data and additional-architecture experiments use the same reported protocols in both versions.

E4.justification: The loss ablations, expert/routing analyses, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, generation-length analysis, mixed-data experiment, and embedding visualizations are retained without revision in Figures 2-5 and Appendices H and K.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical plus/minus uncertainty reporting. Neither version adds or revises run-count or seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or statistical tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative findings match throughout the main text, figures, and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains DeepSeek-V2-Lite Ours scores of 35.59 on MMLU and 49.33 on MATH500; Table 9 retains 11.5 seconds per iteration.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss equations, gradient derivations, two lemmas, and Appendix C.3 proofs and assumptions are identical. No mathematical correction or additional formal result appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about improving expert specialization and downstream performance while maintaining load balance without architectural changes.

C2.justification: Interpretations of loss complementarity, empirical generality, and computational tradeoffs are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations and proposed extensions to visual, multimodal, and distributed settings.

D1.justification: Hardware, implementation instructions, LoRA hyperparameters, dynamic loss scaling, inference settings, and timing information are identical. The embedded code link also has the same target.

R1.justification: Section 5, all 85 reference entries, and the positioning of comparison methods in Appendices G and I are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v4, dated 26 December 2025, to v5, dated 25 January 2026. PDF author metadata adds Xinye Cao, already present in both visible author lists. Prose and section structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1-5, Tables 1-9, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2-36 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in its margin version/date text.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, explanations, and reproducibility information are unchanged throughout both PDFs and their appendices. Updating version identifiers and correcting metadata for an already visibly credited author does not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
